title: Cleaning House
novel: Barney [[convinced|convince]] the gang to help his mother move out of her house. He told them it would be a simple task, but the truth was far more [[complicated|complicated]]. As they packed boxes and sorted through old belongings, Barney [[discovered|discover]] that his mother had been lying to him for years. She had told him stories about his childhood that were [[entirely|entirely]] made up. She wanted to [[protect|protect]] Barney from the painful truth about his father. Barney felt [[betrayed|betray]] at first, but he slowly began to understand his mother's [[intention|intention]]. She had [[sacrificed|sacrifice]] a lot to raise him alone. Meanwhile, Robin had [[oversold|oversell]] Ted to a blind date. She told the woman that Ted was a [[brilliant|brilliant]] architect and a perfect gentleman. When the date actually [[occurred|occur]], Ted could not live up to the [[expectations|expectation]] that Robin had set. He felt [[frustrated|frustrate]] and told Robin that she should not have exaggerated so much. Robin [[apologized|apologize]] and admitted she sometimes got [[carried|carry]] away when she described her friends. Back at the house, the gang finished loading the last boxes. Barney sat on the empty porch and [[reflected|reflect]] on everything he had learned. He realized that his mother's lies came from love, not [[deceit|deceit]]. The gang gathered around him and promised to always be honest with each other. It was a day of [[revelation|revelation]] and growth for everyone.

convince.en: to make someone believe something is true

complicated.en: difficult to understand or deal with

discover.en: to find something for the first time

protect.en: to keep someone or something safe from harm

betray.en: to hurt someone who trusts you

intention.en: a plan or purpose in your mind

sacrifice.en: to give up something valuable for others

oversell.en: to praise something more than it deserves

expectation.en: a belief about what will happen

frustrate.en: to make someone feel annoyed or upset

apologize.en: to say sorry for something you did wrong

carry.en: to take something from one place to another

deceit.en: the act of hiding the truth from people

revelation.en: a surprising fact that is suddenly known
